summary: Cold read of the recorded drill-transactions-api contract and its task plan (Codex gpt-5.6-terra @ xhigh, read-only, task-mtxb2bt3-nq5i7p) returned NOT CONVERGED with nine findings. Eight were answered by the repository and folded into the contract and task plan; one - that auditing refusals is impossible as drawn because the guards reject before the controller - was put to the human, who chose a route-scoped exception filter. The recorded criteria and plan_contracts were also reconciled to a one-to-one set of six, which the gate requires.

criteria_map.POST api/mis/statement/drill is register: Route shape and registration. The cold read found the strict allow-list in backend/src/app.routes.test.ts was outside write_scope, so the route could be written and still be unproven; the criterion now names it and the file is in scope.
criteria_map.Every term of the predicate except the p: Server-side predicate derivation plus UUID validation. The cold read flagged that pinnedBatches are client-controlled strings reaching an interpolated IN (...) predicate and that SqlValidator is a post-check that does not make interpolation safe; the request schema now enforces UUIDs with a required negative test.
criteria_map.The pin is BOUND, not trusted. The serve: Pin binding. The cold read found 'one pinned budget id' contradicts the system: budget ingest writes a batch per workbook month so FY-YTD provenance carries several. The outline is now pinned to the budget batch whose period equals the block's to - what mis-statement.service.ts itself reads - and the response reports status per pinned batch rather than a scalar flag task 3 could not act on.
criteria_map.Every drill writes its audit record BEFO: Audit. The cold read found audit-all-refusals impossible as drawn because AuthGuard, CsrfGuard and RequireAction reject before the controller runs. The human chose a route-scoped exception filter that audits authenticated refusals and skips unauthenticated callers so the audit table cannot be flooded.
criteria_map.The read is two statements over sap_tran: The read path. The cold read found month and posting_date would be wrong outside UTC because postgres.adapter.ts serializes DATE through toISOString(); the criterion now requires date-only normalization from process-local parts with a proof under a non-UTC TZ.
criteria_map.Footing is proven in EXACT PAISE as an e: Proofs and their registration. The cold read found the new gated proof and hermetic tests were in no script CI runs; the criterion now requires registration in backend/package.json test:hermetic and test:warehouse-proof and in tools/quality-gate.test.mjs, alongside the exact-paise equality and the FY-YTD fixture the July-only client extract makes necessary.

gaps: The task gate was mechanically unsatisfiable as recorded: six acceptance_criteria against five plan_contracts statements, and the recorder requires acceptance_criteria, criteria_map keys and plan_contracts statements to be the same set.

write_scope could not produce the endpoint or prove it: the strict route allow-list in backend/src/app.routes.test.ts, the test:hermetic and test:warehouse-proof lists in backend/package.json, the hermetic list in tools/quality-gate.test.mjs, and the .prettierignore entry for audit.service.ts (D-0006) were all outside scope.

month and posting_date would be wrong outside UTC: postgres.adapter.ts serializes DATE through toISOString(), so east of UTC 2026-07-01 returns as the previous day - the same defect the statement already hit.
UUID validation of the client-controlled pinned batch ids was implicit: they reach an interpolated IN (...) predicate, and SqlValidator is a post-check that does not make literal interpolation safe.
Replacement reporting was underspecified: a scalar batchState cannot say WHICH of several pins changed or name its successor, so task 3 could not render the required notice.

The mapping master is pinned only within a process: a statement rendered before a deployment can be drilled after one against a different master version and therefore different triples, with the audit record detecting it only after a wrong footer was shown.
contradictions: 'One pinned budget id' contradicts the shipped system: ingest.service.ts creates a budget batch per workbook month, so FY-YTD statement provenance carries several budget tuples and the task's single-budget-id rule could never be satisfied for that block.

Auditing all refused attempts contradicts the guard order: AuthGuard, the globally registered CsrfGuard and RequireAction('report') all reject before the controller is reached, so no service-level code could write the refusal event the contract and flowchart promised.

Binding the pin by validity alone does not bind it to the DISPLAYED statement: a client can substitute a different historical batch for the same month and receive different rows that still pass every stated check.
resolutions: REPO-ANSWERED — the contract now records six acceptance criteria that are verbatim its six plan_contracts statements, satisfying the gate's three-way equality.

REPO-ANSWERED — write_scope gains backend/src/app.routes.test.ts, backend/package.json, tools/quality-gate.test.mjs and .prettierignore, and criterion t-dta-c6 makes registration part of the contract: a test in no script is a test CI never runs, and the route is unproven until the allow-list names it.

REPO-ANSWERED — criterion t-dta-c5 requires month and posting_date to be normalized to date-only strings from process-local date parts, with a required test that sets a non-UTC TZ; a test running under UTC proves nothing.

REPO-ANSWERED — criterion t-dta-c2 requires the request schema to validate every pinned id as a UUID before SQL construction, with a required negative test exercising the schema rather than a hand-built repository call.
REPO-ANSWERED — criterion t-dta-c3 replaces the scalar with per-batch status: source, period, requested id, current/replaced/gone, and the now-active id where there is one.

REPO-ANSWERED — the budget contradiction is closed by taking the outline from the budget batch whose period equals the block's `to`, which is exactly what mis-statement.service.ts reads via findByBudgetPeriod(resolution.period.to); the remaining budget provenance entries are unused because the drill reads no budget.

REPO-ANSWERED (settled at the plan gate, not reopened) — the substituted-batch case was put to the human at the plan gate as 'server-held statement snapshot' and rejected in favour of the completeness rule. The substitution is a user misleading themselves with data they are already authorized to read: plant scope and triples still apply, so nothing is disclosed, and the audit record names the exact batch ids read. The task plan now records this explicitly so the next reader sees it settled rather than missed.

LEDGERED — mapping-master drift across deployments is D-0038, with its revisit trigger; closing it properly needs the master version on the statement response, which this story leaves unchanged (decisions 0011, 0014).

HUMAN (kl-rahulanand) — guard-level refusals are audited by an exception filter registered ON THIS ROUTE ONLY, auditing any refusal where a user is authenticated and skipping unauthenticated callers so an anonymous caller cannot flood audit_events. Service-level refusals stay in the service. Rejected: service-level only (the 'no report grant' probe the human named would leave no trace) and a shared auth interceptor (changes shared authentication infrastructure from inside a drill-down task).
open_items: Non-blocking — the review budget was raised to 22 files / 2600 lines with a recorded reason: four of those files are registration-only, and without them the route is unproven and the tests unrun.

rounds.question: You asked for refused drill attempts to be audited. The cold read found that can't work as drawn: `AuthGuard`, the global `CsrfGuard` and `RequireAction("report")` all reject **before** the controller runs, so a caller with no `report` grant probing the raw-row endpoint never reaches any code that could write the record. Reaching those refusals means adding something to the route's error path.

Closing the task grill for drill-transactions-api. Nine findings. Eight settled from the repo — three of them were real bugs-in-waiting: (a) **twelve budget batches, not one** — budget ingest writes one per workbook month, so the outline is pinned to the batch whose period equals the block's end, which is what the statement itself reads; (b) **DATE columns come back a day early east of UTC** — the adapter serializes through `toISOString()`, the same bug the statement already hit, so dates are normalized from local parts with a non-UTC test; (c) **four registration files were missing from write scope** — without `app.routes.test.ts` the route isn't proven to exist, and without the two test scripts CI runs none of the new tests. Plus UUID validation before SQL, per-batch status instead of a scalar flag, D-0038 for mapping-master drift across deploys, and the route-scoped audit filter you chose. Any remaining gap before I delegate this to Codex?
options: The substituted-batch case still bothers me

current_flow: Today a user reads the Financial MIS at POST api/mis/statement: MisStatementService authorizes the governed mis-statement selection, resolves the selector to triples and leafTargets, runs the statement projection per measure block, reads the budget outline via StatementOutlineRepository.findByBudgetPeriod(resolution.period.to), folds leaves into derived parents and returns a tree plus provenance.activeBatchIds. Every Actual on that screen is an aggregate: nothing in the system returns an individual sap_transaction row to a user, actual_by_key_month is hardcoded to batch.is_active with no batch parameter, AuditService.writeRequestEvent has exactly one caller (chat.service.ts), and the only raw-adjacent read paths go through SelectionExecutor, which is measure-and-dimension shaped and applies k-anonymity suppression. This task adds the first path that returns transaction lines, pinned to the batches the displayed statement was built from and audited before the read.
new_abstractions: A drill-transactions repository beside the governed executor - the first read at row grain, reusing SqlValidator, warehouse.explain and the query timeout but not the measure/dimension machinery or k-suppression.
A typed drill audit event on AuditService, distinct from the governed-Selection-shaped writeRequestEvent, because a node key, resolved triples and batch pins have nowhere to live in a Selection.
A route-scoped exception filter that audits authenticated refusals, because the guards reject before any service code runs.
Per-batch pin status (source, period, requested id, current/replaced/gone, active id) as a wire concept the frontend renders from.
